title: An unconditional first moment for cubic Gauss sums
main_claim: Without assuming GRH, the sum of G(pi) over primary Eisenstein primes with N(pi) <= X equals (6/5) c_* X^{5/6}/log X + o(X^{5/6}/log X), where c_* = (2pi)^{2/3}/(3 Gamma(2/3)). This is Patterson's first-moment conjecture, which Dunn-Radziwill proved under GRH. The paper also proves o(X^{5/6}/log X) cancellation for every fixed nonzero angular twist, and hence for G(pi)^k when 3 does not divide k and |k| > 1.

issues.location: sections/background-type1.tex, Theorem 2.6 (metaplectic mean-square input, eq. hb-mean-square)
issues.description: The level exponent (Nr)^{1/2+4eps} T^2 is imported from Heath-Brown 2000 Section 3 Lemma 3, and I could not check it offline. The upper-block Type I bound X^{1/2} R^{3/4} T^{1/2} depends on it exactly; an R^1 dependence would push the exponent above 5/6 at R ~ X^{1/3}, T ~ X^{1/6}. However, Lemma A.3 (angular appendix, completed sums at large heights) derives the same sqrt(V) R^{1/4} sqrt(T) bound independently from the Dunn-Radziwill level Voronoi formula. That derivation covers l=0, which corroborates the input. Not a gap, only a dependency on a cited bound that I did not check.
issues.evidence: int_{-T}^T |f_r(1/2+eps+it)|^2 dt << (Nr)^{1/2+4eps} T^2 ... The mean-square assertion is [HB2000, Section 3, Lemma 3]

coverage:
I read all of main.tex and every section file: background and Type I, dual, dispersion, decomposition, perron, and the angular appendix.

Checked in detail:
- Prop 3.1, the new unconditional ingredient. I checked the dominant-full-sum dual length (Y^{0.72}) and the bound Y^{2.16} < 7/3. I checked the second-configuration inequalities r+4v<=4 and r<=2/3 (forcing v=5/6) and the contradiction from an extra factor. In the first configuration I checked the multiplicity inequality r <= 2/3 - 2 sum k_i d_i, the identity z + 2(1+z)/3 = 2/3 + 5z/3 on [1/2,2], the step forcing d_i=0, the choice of a power with z in (4/3,2), and the BHM/Gram gaps (2-z)/3, (3z-4)/6 and (z-1)/6.
- Gram Lemma 3.3: amplitude, J_0, and the three substituted terms ZP/(MK), P^2/K^2, P^2 Z^{1/3}/(K^2 M^{1/3}).
- Both extensions of the cubic large sieve (inner and outer factorizations).
- In dispersion: the ratio tables for the P-dominant, Q-dominant and equal cases. The two exceptional configurations are exactly those covered by Prop 3.1, with f=l=1, B=X^{1/2+o(1)} and |u'| <= B^{0.36}. I checked the scaling of the cube-frequency lattice sum and verified the Riesz constant equals c_*^2 independently.
- Type I: completion-error exponents .795, .805, .755, .77 and 5/6-1/50; the identity A_0 = c_* * 2pi/(9 sqrt3); the high-height bound X^{1/2} R^{3/4} T^{1/2}.
- Decomposition: the exact prime detector, the subset-sum grouping lemma, the binomial-weight separation at the stopping bin and its crossing predicate, the Rankin bound for sparse late stops, and the norm ranges for Type I and Type II on both block types.
- Perron assembly: the 1+X/T truncation, the near and far cell sums, the q-fold integration by parts, the parameter ordering, and the three-prime transition bound X^{5/6} L^{-3/2} (log L)^C.
- Angular appendix: Lemma A.3, and G(pi)^3 = -theta_1(pi), which I verified against Ireland-Rosen under the paper's convention that primary means = 1 mod 3.

Numerical check: the sum of S_p/(2 sqrt p) over p = 1 mod 3 up to 4e5, divided by c_* times the sum of p^{-1/6}, is 0.985. This supports the main-term constant.

Not independently verified: the exact Dunn-Radziwill Voronoi coefficients and residue (Proposition 5.3), and the exponent in Heath-Brown's Lemma 3.
